citation: Moses et al. — Reverse-mode automatic differentiation and optimization of GPU kernels via Enzyme
reviewed_sections: AD construction; GPU memory/synchronization; evaluation and artifact appendix
finding: LLVM-level differentiation generates GPU gradients; Rust is among the compatible source-language frontends.
limitation: GPU-kernel results do not establish a native Rust breast-cancer training benchmark.
project_decision: Require analytical or finite-difference gradient checks before a separately planned native-training experiment.

citation: Li and Bezemer — Bridging the language gap: an empirical study of bindings
reviewed_sections: Binding detection; release coverage and technical lag; threats to validity
finding: Cross-ecosystem bindings often cover limited host-library releases and lag behind upstream changes.
limitation: An ecosystem inventory does not measure Rust model accuracy or deployment speed.
project_decision: Pin binding, host runtime and native dependencies together; test the restored environment.

citation: Li et al. — Studying the impact of TensorFlow and PyTorch bindings on ML software quality
finding: Pretrained models retained assessed accuracy across studied bindings, while training outcomes and runtimes varied.
limitation: Historical TensorFlow 2.5.0/PyTorch 1.9.0; accuracy agreement does not establish probability or calibration parity.
project_decision: Preserve our per-specimen probability comparison before any Rust runtime benchmark.

citation: Zhang et al. — A fast, scalable and versatile tool for analysis of single-cell omics data
reviewed_sections: Matrix-free embedding; Rust/Python architecture; selected single-cell evaluations; availability
finding: SnapATAC2 combines Rust subroutines and a Python interface for scalable single-cell representation analysis.
limitation: Cell embeddings and tissue composition do not validate a patient-level breast-cancer prediction endpoint.
project_decision: Define cell/specimen/donor identities and an out-of-sample representation boundary before extending the book.

citation: Luo et al. — Benchmarking computational methods for single-cell chromatin data analysis
reviewed_sections: Benchmark design; SnapATAC2 2.2.0 preprocessing; clustering settings; availability
finding: Independent evaluation compares single-cell methods across representations, graphs and clustering metrics.
limitation: A method-level benchmark is not a controlled Rust-versus-Python runtime experiment.
project_decision: Separate biological representation quality, resource use and patient-level prediction assessment.

citation: Carnelos et al. — MicroFlow: an efficient Rust-based inference engine for TinyML
reviewed_sections: Compiler/quantization design; memory allocation; selected MCU evaluations; conclusions
finding: Compile-time model processing and quantized operators support Rust inference on constrained microcontrollers.
limitation: Results depend on supported operators, quantization and devices; no assay-specific clinical validation.
project_decision: Assess conversion and a new precision contract before any embedded version of the assay model.

citation: Drehwald et al. — MOLPIPx: differentiable polynomials in Python and Rust
reviewed_sections: Polynomial translation; JAX/Enzyme backends; example scope and future work
finding: Python and Rust derivative paths support molecular potential models; reviewed Rust examples are limited to linear models.
limitation: Molecular energies are not breast-cancer outcomes; manuscript v2 is not a full audit of the published supplement.
project_decision: Keep a molecular-model learning case separate from the current tissue-category and future prognosis endpoints.

citation: Liang et al. — ad-trait: a fast and flexible automatic differentiation library in Rust
reviewed_sections: Trait implementation; gradient/Jacobian benchmarks; robotics evaluation; limitations
finding: Trait-based forward/reverse differentiation is assessed on numerical functions and robotics optimization.
limitation: Scalar reverse-mode overhead and integration costs limit transfer to tensor-heavy neural training.
project_decision: Use controlled derivative checks and record objective, precision and optimization budgets for native training.

citation: Khan et al. — Performance evaluation of ML applications using WebAssembly across languages
reviewed_sections: K-means/logistic implementations; browser/WASI experiments; discussion and future work
finding: Logistic and clustering experiments compare Rust, Python and C++ under browser and WASI runtimes.
limitation: Synthetic workloads and unequal dependency support confound broad language-speed conclusions.
project_decision: A browser extension needs probability parity, compatible preprocessing and a declared workload before timing.

citation: Huang et al. — Ariel-ML: embedded Rust leveraging multicore for neural networks
reviewed_sections: Build pipeline; Rust/IREE runtime boundary; scheduler; device-specific evaluation
finding: Rust orchestration combines with an IREE C runtime and multicore scheduling for MCU inference.
limitation: Hybrid runtime/device results are not evidence for a wholly Rust stack or breast-cancer model accuracy.
project_decision: Inventory native runtimes and hardware alongside the Rust binary before a future edge deployment.

citation: Adito — Training a language model end-to-end in Rust: an experience report
reviewed_version: arXiv PDF v1 dated 2026-07-27; landing-page metadata unavailable
reviewed_sections: Framework failure taxonomy 3; verification 3.3; results context; artifacts 9; data statement 10
finding: One author reports backend/gradient failures and advocates explicit checks before expensive training.
limitation: Unreplicated single-project preprint; full training stack/logs are on request and weights are unreleased.
project_decision: Check expected gradient paths and numerical agreement; nonzero gradients for every parameter are not a universal validity rule.

finding: The inspected binary logistic implementation exposes probabilities and an explicit L2-weighted objective.
limitation: A source inspection does not establish successful compilation, grouped assessment or penalty equivalence to scikit-learn.
project_decision: First native-training candidate: declare the objective and person-grouped fit contract before implementation.

finding: The inspected logistic predict path returns class labels rather than a saved probability table.
limitation: This selected file review is not an exhaustive audit of probability interfaces throughout the crate.
project_decision: Verify a probability interface and class direction before using this learner with Brier selection.

reviewed_sections: Train/validation loaders; seeded training; stopping; checkpoint/config saving
finding: The example has train/validation loaders, early stopping and model/config persistence.
limitation: MNIST partitions and stopping rules do not supply donor-grouped assay validation.
project_decision: Replace row-oriented example partitions with person-grouped inner training/validation slices.

reviewed_sections: VarMap and optimizer; backward step; per-epoch test reporting; weight save/load
finding: The example makes optimization and persistence explicit and reports MNIST test accuracy each epoch.
limitation: Copying per-epoch test monitoring into the protected assay test would compromise its role if used for choices.
project_decision: Monitor an inner validation set; reserve final-test people until all stopping and model choices are frozen.

reviewed_sections: Session construction; graph execution interface and native session ownership
finding: Session runs an ONNX graph through a native ONNX Runtime interface.
limitation: Our current numeric JSON is not an ONNX model; graph conversion and runtime support remain untested.
project_decision: Require end-to-end preprocessing conversion, runtime pinning and per-specimen probability parity.

finding: The documentation describes experimental compiler differentiation with an Enzyme-capable toolchain.
limitation: This is not enabled by the repository's pinned stable Rust inference toolchain.
project_decision: Keep compiler experiments in a separate declared environment; retain the working inference deployment.
